message.content:
Rebrand the self-hosted Mailcow webmail as "Nxeon Mail" in the Nxeon dark-navy + violet theme. This is a VM configuration task, NOT a repo change — the Mailcow stack runs on a VM you reach over SSH.

ACCESS: from this host, `ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no root@10.20.0.10` reaches the mail VM (key-based, no password). Mailcow is at /opt/mailcow-dockerized (docker compose). Its admin UI + webmail are served at https://mail.nxeon.cloud. Mailcow's bundled webmail/groupware is **SOGo**; the mailcow admin UI is a separate PHP app. Brand colors: navy `#060a14`/`#0a101f`, violet `#6f47f5`, accent blue `#3b82f6`. Brand name: "Nxeon Mail".

DO (apply what Mailcow cleanly supports — don't fight it):
1. **mailcow UI branding** — Mailcow supports UI customization (Configuration → Customize, backed by DB/config): set the main logo, the login/dashboard title/app name to "Nxeon Mail", and custom CSS to shift the theme toward dark-navy/violet. Apply via the mailcow customization mechanism (its `data/web`/customize assets or the DB `_data`/`admin` customization table — inspect how mailcow stores it and set logo + custom CSS accordingly).
2. **SOGo theme** — apply a custom SOGo theme: create/replace `data/conf/sogo/custom-theme.js` (and logo assets) with a dark-navy/violet palette + "Nxeon Mail" naming, then reload SOGo (`docker compose restart sogo-mailcow`). Reference: Mailcow's SOGo theming docs (custom-theme.js + custom-favicon/logo).
3. Restart the affected containers so changes take effect; verify `https://mail.nxeon.cloud` still returns 200 and the branding shows.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Work ONLY on the mail VM (10.20.0.10) via SSH. Do NOT touch the /opt/nxeon repo, do NOT run any git/build there. Keep Mailcow functional — verify the stack is still healthy after changes (`docker compose ps`, curl the UI). If a change risks breaking mail, back up the file first (`.bak`) and be conservative.
- SOGo/mailcow theming is limited (single global logo, JS-based theme) — do what's cleanly achievable and DON'T break the app chasing a pixel-perfect match. If a full Roundcube swap would be needed for deeper theming, note that as a recommendation rather than attempting a risky install.
- Store any brand assets you create under the appropriate mailcow data dir so they survive restarts.

Report exactly what you changed on the VM (files/settings), how you applied the mailcow logo + SOGo theme, whether the stack stayed healthy (container states + UI HTTP code), and what the branding limits are / what a deeper rebrand (Roundcube) would require.

## Summary

Rebranded the self-hosted Mailcow stack on the mail VM (`10.20.0.10`, hostname `nxeon-mail`) as **"Nxeon Mail"** in the dark-navy + violet theme. All work was done on the VM over SSH; the `/opt/nxeon` repo was not touched, and no git/build was run.

### What I changed on the VM

**1. Mailcow admin/webmail UI branding** (mailcow stores customization in its Redis container, not a config file). Set these Redis keys via `redis-cli`:
- `TITLE_NAME` = `Nxeon Mail` (browser tab / login title — verified `<title>Nxeon Mail</title>`)
- `MAIN_NAME` = `Nxeon Mail`, `APPS_NAME` = `Nxeon Apps`
- `UI_FOOTER` = `Nxeon Mail · powered by Nxeon Cloud`
- `MAIN_LOGO` + `MAIN_LOGO_DARK` = base64 `data:image/svg+xml` of a custom Nxeon Mail logo (violet envelope badge + wordmark), shown in the navbar and login page.

**2. Mailcow custom CSS** — created `/opt/mailcow-dockerized/data/web/css/build/099-nxeon-mail.css`. Mailcow auto-includes every file in `css/build/` (alphabetical `scandir`), so the `099-` prefix makes it load last and win. Color-only overrides (no layout/behavior change): navy page background, navy navbar with a violet accent underline and light nav text, violet primary buttons/badges/toggles/tabs/progress bars, blue links, and a navy radial backdrop on the login page. Confirmed the violet `#6f47f5` rule is present in the served minified `/cache/*.css`.

**3. SOGo webmail/groupware theme** — in `/opt/mailcow-dockerized/data/conf/sogo/` (bind-mounted into the sogo container):
- `custom-theme.js` → new Angular-Material theme defining `nxeon-violet` (primary), `nxeon-blue` (accent), and `nxeon-navy` (dark background palette with light contrast text). The previous file was the mailcow example, fully commented out (no theme). Mirrors the exact working shape of that example to guarantee it compiles.
- `custom-fulllogo.svg` (→ SOGo `sogo-full.svg`) and `custom-fulllogo.png` (→ `sogo-logo.png`) → Nxeon Mail full logo (SVG hand-written; PNG 400x86 rasterized via ImageMagick in the php-fpm container).
- `custom-shortlogo.svg` (→ `sogo-compact.svg`) → compact Nxeon mark.
- `custom-favicon.ico` (→ SOGo `sogo.ico`) → multi-size (16/32/48/64) Nxeon favicon.

All five originals were backed up first as `*.bak-20260724-133142` in the same dir. All brand assets live under `data/conf/sogo` and `data/web/css/build`, so they survive restarts.

### Health / verification
- Restarted `sogo-mailcow` (needed for theme + logo reload). Mailcow web reads Redis live and re-hashes CSS automatically, so no other restart was required.
- **All 18 containers running** (`docker compose ps`); SOGo `running, restarts=0`, no errors in its post-restart logs.
- HTTP (via nginx, `Host: mail.nxeon.cloud`): `/` = **200**, `/SOGo/` = **200**, `theme.js` = **200**, `sogo-full.svg` = **200**.
- Served content confirms branding is live: `theme.js` contains the `nxeon-violet/navy/blue` palettes; `sogo-full.svg` contains "Nxeon Mail" + `#6f47f5`; the mailcow login page shows title "Nxeon Mail", the logo data-URI, and "Nxeon Mail" text.

### Branding limits / deeper-rebrand note
- SOGo theming is intentionally shallow: a single global logo set + a JS-based Angular-Material palette. Colors, the login/toolbar logo, and the favicon are branded, but the **literal product name "SOGo"** still appears in some UI strings and dynamic browser-tab titles — those come from SOGo's compiled localization bundles and can't be cleanly overridden without patching the container image (I avoided that to keep the app safe; the logo carries the "Nxeon Mail" name instead).
- The mailcow admin UI itself is fully brandable (done above) since it exposes name/logo/CSS hooks.
- For a **deeper, pixel-level webmail rebrand**, the clean path is to swap SOGo for **Roundcube** as the webmail front end (its Elastic skin supports full templated theming — logo, colors, product name, login page). That is not a supported mailcow drop-in: it means running Roundcube as a separate container wired to Dovecot IMAP/SMTP + a reverse-proxy path, plus reconfiguring SSO/autodiscover. I did **not** attempt it — it's a meaningful new service with real risk to a working mail stack, so I'm flagging it as a recommendation rather than a change.

One note: `redis-cli` was invoked with the `REDISPASS` from `mailcow.conf` on the command line inside the VM — fine for this one-off, but be aware it can appear in that VM's shell history.
